_doc: THE ELEMENT-DISPATCH LEDGER. See scripts/check_element_dispatch.py for what
this is and why it exists. Every function that switches on Element kind with
no container arm must appear here exactly once.
VERDICTS:
leaf_only -- the container case IS handled; `handled_at` says where.
unhandled -- containers have NO answer anywhere; `unreached_because` says
what keeps them away, and `becomes_owed_when` states the
expiry. NOT a decision to reject containers -- an unfinished
feature with a note saying so.
owed      -- a container DOES reach here and the result is wrong or
silently nothing; `artist_visible` says what they see.
Five defects wore this shape in one week, every one invisible in Rust (where
doc.set_selection expands containers) and live in JasSwift (which does not).
LAYER_STRUCTURE.md section 20 removes that expansion, at which point every
remaining site goes live in Rust too.
OWED TO THIS LEDGER: FALSIFIABLE CLAIMS. As of 2026-07-29 a row's `reason`,
`artist_visible` and `evidence` are checked for PRESENCE and non-blankness,
never for truth -- and two of this seat's first three `owed` rows named a
production read path that did not exist. The sibling gate
check_widget_kind_dispatch.py now carries the fix: each exemption states its
argument as {file, contains|lacks} claims that are VERIFIED every run, so an
argument cannot outlive the condition it describes. See `verify_asserts`
there; the reusable law is in widget_dispatch_exemptions.json's _doc.
NOT ADOPTED HERE YET, deliberately and with a trigger rather than an
open-ended someday. The one surviving `owed` row rests on a claim about the
PRINT path ('the PDF/print exporter has NO counter-scale'), and pinning that
as a machine-checked anchor means tracing the exporter properly. Guessing the
anchor would produce exactly the confident-and-wrong row this mechanism
exists to prevent, which is a poor way to introduce it.
TRIGGER: adopt `asserts` on the NEXT `owed` row added or resolved, whichever
comes first. At that moment someone is already reading the print path with
reason to be sure.

rust:jas_dioxus/src/geometry/element.rs:.reason: An accessor for an element's OWN fill, and a container genuinely has none. The container answer belongs to the SUMMARY that reads a selection, and as of 2026-07-29 selection_fill_summary recurses to paintable leaves, so a group reads back its members' common value or Mixed.
As fill: the container answer lives in selection_stroke_summary.

Containers have NO answer here, and it costs nothing today because NOTHING in production asks. This row previously read `owed` with the consequence "set a gradient on a group, and the Gradient panel reads back empty" -- written by this seat WITHOUT tracing the read path, and DISPROVEN when it was traced. The Gradient panel has no production read path in EITHER port: its panel.* scope is the declared gradient.yaml defaults for every selection, so a gradient-filled LEAF, a solid leaf and a group all display linear / 0 deg / 100% / classic / black->white, byte-identical (driven, both ports). Not a container defect, and not 'empty' either -- a plausible default an artist could mistake for the real value.
rust:jas_dioxus/src/geometry/element.rs:.unreached_because: The only non-render production reader would be AppState::sync_gradient_panel_from_selection, which the Rust compiler reports as never used -- its three call sites all sit inside #[cfg(test)] mod tests (renderer.rs:10740). The Swift twin syncGradientPanelFromSelection is likewise called only from Tests/Interpreter/GradientPanelSyncTests.swift. The accessor's remaining production reader is the RENDER path, where returning None for a group is CORRECT -- a group has no fill of its own to paint.
rust:jas_dioxus/src/geometry/element.rs:.becomes_owed_when: the Gradient panel gains a production read path (a live panel-override block, as the Color and Stroke panels have) -- at which point a container summary twin is needed here, alongside selection_fill_summary.
rust:jas_dioxus/src/geometry/element.rs:.evidence: driven in both ports by an adversarially-verified trace, 2026-07-29

rust:jas_dioxus/src/geometry/element.rs:.reason: As fill_gradient, and disproven the same way. A stroke-gradient LEAF does not round-trip either: through the accessor plus the test-only sync it round-trips perfectly (radial / 37 deg / 250% / smooth / dither / across), and through the path the application actually uses it shows the gradient.yaml defaults -- identical to what a group shows. The two answers differ by WHICH PATH YOU ASK, which is the whole finding.

rust:jas_dioxus/src/document/op_apply.rs.reason: THE ONE OF THIS SEAT'S THREE `owed` CLAIMS THAT SURVIVED TRACING. A container reaches here through the transform trio and its members' stored stroke widths are left untouched. Sharpened by the trace: the canvas renderer DELIBERATELY counter-scales descendant stroke widths by the ancestor-transform chain (render.rs:558 / CanvasSubwindow.swift:325), so scale_strokes ON and OFF are literally INDISTINGUISHABLE on canvas for a selected group -- not merely a stored/rendered mismatch. The closed variant list also misses Element::Live, so a compound-shape LEAF is missed too, and there the ports DIVERGE (Swift bakes, Rust does not) -- a prime-directive violation independent of containers. Prerequisite for the transform box (transcripts/TRANSFORM_BOX.md section 9).
rust:jas_dioxus/src/document/op_apply.rs.artist_visible: Scale a group 2x with scale_strokes on and the canvas looks correct while the stored numbers disagree -- but the PDF/print exporter has NO counter-scale, so the same document prints with unscaled member strokes. Canvas and print disagree.
rust:jas_dioxus/src/document/op_apply.rs.evidence: driven in both ports, and adversarially verified; the print-path exception was found by the refuter, not the tracer, 2026-07-29

It is called on every node of the tree during the render walk, containers included, and the walk descends into children on its own -- so a container's own answer is about the container's own paint, which is the right question.
